# n6 - Answer, proposals, and rewind

Three things that write the graph rather than read it.

`runner answer --node d1 --decision "..."` closes a decision node: the text goes into `graph.md`
`## Decisions` through `GraphFile.append_decision`, the node gets a `done` line with
`verdict=answered`, and the verb prints what became ready (C26).

`RunnerProposals` accepts or refuses what an executor proposed (C8). The runner mints every id
(D28). A proposed edge is accepted only when both endpoints exist, the head is not `running`, and
the result stays acyclic (D30); a refusal writes one ledger comment naming which of the three
failed, and nothing is partially written.

`answer` also unparks a work node the runner parked at `needs_decision` (D22). Below the hard
attempt backstop it writes `planned`; at or above it, it supersedes the node and mints a successor
carrying the same body, files and edges. Superseding is the only exit the shipped ledger offers,
because only `done`, `superseded` and `abandoned` reset the attempt count.

`runner rewind --node n3 --confirm` resets the intent branch to a node's recorded commit, marks
every downstream node superseded, and respins the rewound node the same way `answer` does, rather
than writing `planned` (D22): `failed_verification_count` never resets, so a node rewound after two
failures would be parked again by the retry cap on its first dispatch. Rewind is internal and
confirm-gated: the graph facts it needs are here, and publishing it before G10 has measured a real
run would invite a reset nobody has evidence for.

## n6 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Write the answer into `graph.md` `## Decisions` | The decision lives only in the ledger and the next packet never carries it | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_appends_to_graph_decisions` |
| 6.2 | Close the decision node with `verdict=answered` | The decision node stays open and its successors never become ready | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_writes_done_with_verdict` |
| 6.3 | Print what became ready after the answer | The owner answers and is not told the loop can continue | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_prints_newly_ready_nodes` |
| 6.4 | Refuse `answer` on a work node that is not parked at `needs_decision` | A work node is closed by hand with no evidence at all | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_refuses_healthy_work_node` |
| 6.4a | Unpark a work node parked at `needs_decision` below the hard cap (D22, meld of blocker 3) | `READY_PRIOR_STATES` holds only `planned` and `failed_verification`, so a parked node can never be dispatched again and the run stalls forever | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_unparks_parked_work_node_to_planned` |
| 6.4b | Respin a parked node at or above the hard attempt cap | Writing `planned` clears nothing, because only a terminal line resets `attempts_count`, so the node is refused at exit 5 on its next dispatch | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_respins_node_at_hard_cap` |
| 6.4c | Carry the superseded node's body, files and edges onto the successor | The respun node loses its matrix and its declared surface, and the diff-scope check has nothing to check against | `runner_answer_test#test_respin_successor_inherits_body_files_and_edges` |
| 6.4d | Record `by=` on the superseded line | `superseded` requires `by`, so the append raises and the respin leaves the graph half-written | `runner_answer_test#test_supersede_line_carries_by_field` |
| 6.5 | Refuse `answer` on a decision node that is already done | A second answer overwrites the first and the record shows only the later one | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_refuses_already_answered_node` |
| 6.6 | Refuse an empty decision text | An empty decision closes the node and the graph records nothing | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_refuses_empty_decision` |
| 6.7 | Write `graph.md` through temp-plus-rename | A crash mid-write truncates the graph and the whole intent becomes unreadable | `runner_answer_test#test_graph_write_is_atomic` |
| 6.8 | Mint a proposed node's id | An executor picks an id, collides with an existing node, and two nodes share a subject in the ledger | `runner_proposals_test#test_runner_mints_proposed_node_id` |
| 6.9 | Substitute the minted id in all three places the template hard-codes `n1` (D29, meld of major 18) | The frontmatter key, the H1 and the `## n1 failure-mode matrix` heading all still say `n1`, so `has_valid_matrix?` fails and `validate` reports a duplicate node id | `runner_proposals_test#test_scaffold_substitutes_minted_id_everywhere` |
| 6.9a | Take `files` and `budget` from the proposal, or from the kind's default | The scaffold keeps the template's placeholder path and the diff-scope check compares against `path/to/file.rb` | `runner_proposals_test#test_scaffold_takes_files_and_budget_from_proposal` |
| 6.9b | Re-run the full validator after an accepted proposal (meld of major 19) | The validator is skipped after the first dispatch, so a mid-run scaffold with a missing section is never checked and row 6.9's stated consequence cannot occur | `runner_proposals_test#test_validator_reruns_after_accepted_proposal` |
| 6.10 | Append the proposed node to `## Graph` as planned | The node file exists and the graph declares no such node, which the validator calls an error | `runner_proposals_test#test_proposed_node_appended_to_graph` |
| 6.11 | Refuse a proposed edge whose endpoint does not exist | A dangling edge lands and the ready function blocks on a node that was never declared | `runner_proposals_test#test_edge_to_unknown_node_is_refused` |
| 6.12 | Refuse a proposed edge into a `running` node | An edge changes the rules under a node that is already executing | `runner_proposals_test#test_edge_into_running_node_is_refused` |
| 6.13 | Refuse a proposed edge that makes a cycle | Two nodes wait on each other and the loop stalls with an empty ready set | `runner_proposals_test#test_cyclic_edge_is_refused` |
| 6.14 | Write one ledger comment naming the refusal reason | A refusal is silent and the executor proposes the same edge every attempt | `runner_proposals_test#test_refusal_records_reason` |
| 6.15 | Write nothing when any part of a proposal is refused | Half a proposal lands and the graph is left in a shape nobody authored | `runner_proposals_test#test_refused_proposal_writes_nothing` |
| 6.16 | Refuse `rewind` without `--confirm` | A reset runs by accident and committed work is gone | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_requires_confirm` |
| 6.17 | Reset the intent branch to the node's recorded commit | The reset targets the wrong commit and the branch loses work the node did not produce | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_resets_to_node_commit` |
| 6.18 | Mark every downstream node superseded | Downstream nodes stay done while the code they were built on is gone | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_supersedes_downstream_nodes` |
| 6.19 | Respin the rewound node rather than writing `planned` (D22, meld of major 20) | `failed_verification_count` never resets, so a node rewound after two failures is parked again by the retry cap on its very first dispatch | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_respins_instead_of_planning` |
| 6.19a | Reset the successor's cap counters through the supersede | The respun node inherits the old node's failure history and is unrunnable | `runner_rewind_test#test_respun_node_starts_with_clean_counters` |
| 6.20 | Refuse `rewind` on a node with no recorded commit | The reset targets nil and the branch moves somewhere arbitrary | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_refuses_node_without_commit` |
| 6.21 | Refuse `rewind` while any node is `running` | A live executor's branch base moves under it mid-node | `runner_rewind_test#test_rewind_refuses_while_a_node_runs` |
| 6.22 | Re-render `graph.md` `## Status` after answering, respinning or rewinding (D28) | The Status table contradicts the ledger the moment the graph is written | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_rerenders_graph_status` |
| 6.23 | Register `runner_answer.rb`, `runner_proposals.rb` and `runner_rewind.rb` in `core_files` (D25) | `install_sync_test` goes red as soon as `scripts/runner` requires them | `install_sync_test#test_core_files_match_disk` |
| 6.24 | Keep `runner_cli_test` row 1.6 honest once every verb is delivered (lead ruling, attempt 3) | `test_missing_module_fails_only_its_own_verb` used `rewind` as its undelivered example; n6 delivers `rewind`, so the row asserts `not yet delivered` against a verb that now loads and the whole suite goes red | `runner_cli_test#test_missing_module_fails_only_its_own_verb` |

1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code.
2. Write `RunnerAnswer`, `RunnerProposals` and `RunnerRewind`, and wire their subcommands.
3. Green, then the whole suite at its baseline.
